request: Analyze GSE281849 for PMID 39609254 (Inactivity-mediated molecular adaptations: Insights from a preclinical model of physical activity reduction.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk poly(A) RNA-seq, gastrocnemius medial belly, female C57BL/6NJ mice (S2.11.p1, S3.7.p1, FIG3)

group: Activity Reduction (treadmill 4 wk then 2 wk inactive)

final.sample_inclusion: RNA-seq on female mice only, n = 7 per group (S3.7.p1, FIG3 legend); males not sequenced
final.primary_estimand: Effect of regular treadmill exercise on the gastrocnemius transcriptome (Active vs Inactive), plus the effect of 2 weeks of activity reduction relative to the inactive and active controls
planned_contrasts: Activity Reduction vs Inactive (FIG3b; paper: 40 DEGs)
Activity Reduction vs Active (FIG3c; paper: 124 DEGs)
final.repeated_measure_unit: none; one sample per independent mouse
final.paper_method: DESeq2 ~ group, each pairwise comparison fitted on the two groups' samples only (authors' Figure 3.Rmd: subset columns, design ~group, results(contrast=...), no lfcShrink, rowSums>0 prefilter)
final.paper_results: 71/40/124 DEGs (S3.7.p1); 7 transcripts unique to Activity Reduction (Smyd2, En1, Hoxa11os up; Ostn, Ak4, Srrm4os, Zfhx4 down); Igfbp5 down in Active and AR vs Inactive; 16 Active-unique transcripts (S3.7.p1)

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: S2.3.p1 defines the three randomized groups; S2.11.p1 gives DESeq2 and 'FDR<0.05 and the fold change was >0.25 in either direction'; FIG3 legend says 'q < 0.05 and expression change >= 20%'; S3.7.p1 gives the DEG counts on female gastrocnemius n=7/group. The authors' public Figure 3.Rmd (DA.p1 link) fits each pairwise comparison separately with design ~group and calls DEGs at padj<=0.05 and |log2FC|>=0.27.

checks: 21 GEO samples = 7 per group, female gastrocnemius, matches FIG3 legend n=21
GEO data_processing (fastp, STAR GRCm39, featureCounts, DESeq2) matches S2.11.p1
sample IDs M304-M325 match the columns in the authors' Figure 3.Rmd and their group lists

ownership.reasoning: DA.p1 names GSE281849; samples, tissue and processing agree with the paper and the authors' code.

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns (M304...) equal the metadata 'description' field for all 21 samples (inspect alignment_keys). Group from characteristics treatment: SED = inactive control, ACT = active control, AR = activity reduction. The resulting sample lists equal the authors' code lists (AR = M307,M310,M314,M318,M320,M321,M322; Active = M304,M305,M306,M308,M309,M312,M319).

candidates.reason_rejected: DESeq2-normalized values; DESeq2 needs the raw counts

matrix.reasoning: All values integer, 0 to 4.7e6; file named RawCounts; GEO data_processing: featureCounts, 'csv file includes raw counts for each sample'. Matches the paper's input.

candidates.reason_rejected: the paper keeps three groups and the AR arm is defined by detraining; pooling changes the estimand

design.reasoning: Three randomized independent groups (S2.3.p1). The exercise effect is Active vs Inactive (primary); Activity Reduction vs Inactive and vs Active are the paper's other planned contrasts (FIG3b,c). All female, so no sex split.

covariance.reasoning: Independent mice randomized to groups (S2.3.p1); no batch, lane or litter recorded in GEO; the paper models group only.

final.method: DESeq2 (pydeseq2 Wald), separate fit per pairwise comparison
deviations: pydeseq2 instead of R DESeq2; the authors prefilter rowSums>0, which does not change DESeq2 results for kept genes

method.reasoning: Raw counts support the paper's DESeq2. The authors' code fits each comparison on its two groups only, so each execution subsets to the two groups. A joint 3-group model is run as a sensitivity analysis.

final.deviation_note: Methods text S2.11.p1 ('FDR<0.05 and fold change >0.25 in either direction', read as |log2FC| > 0.25) is applied. FIG3 legend says >=20% change (|log2FC| >= 0.263); the authors' code uses padj<=0.05 and |log2FC|>=0.27, recorded as the audit rule.

threshold.reasoning: S2.11.p1 states the DEG rule; FIG3 legend and the authors' code give near-equal variants, kept as an audit rule.

caveats: Female mice only; the effect of exercise in males is not assessed by this dataset.
Paper's GSEA used GO BP with fgsea; this run's GSEA uses MSigDB Hallmark, so pathway results are not directly comparable.

study.reasoning: Paper-aligned DESeq2 pairwise route on the deposited raw counts; compare counts and named genes from S3.7.p1.

discrepancies.paper: S2.11.p1: fold change >0.25; FIG3 legend: >=20% change
fgsea on GO Biological Process, FDR<0.25

executions.name: grp_ACT_vs_SED
executions.reasoning: FIG3a Active vs Inactive, fitted on these 14 samples as in the authors' code

executions.name: joint
executions.reasoning: one 3-group DESeq2 model on all 21 samples, to check robustness of the pairwise fits

enrichment.reasoning: paper reports GSEA for Active vs Inactive (S3.7.p2)
paper reports GSEA for Activity Reduction vs Active (S3.7.p2)
